title: End-to-End Reference Architecture: Visual Guide
outline: Title: End-to-End Reference Architecture: Visual Guide

1. Six Stages, One Document | the source-to-serving flow as six tappable stages — which earlier course built each one, what it holds, and where the 40-page PDF is at 14:00, 14:07 and 14:32 | nothing here is new machinery; the lesson is the conveyor between parts you already own, and bronze/silver are the corpus of record while everything downstream is derived

2. Batch Or Streaming | 8,000 document edits, 40 ACL/deletion events and 300 price updates a day, each toggled onto a path, with the streaming record count and the revocation exposure recomputed | freshness x volume x cost is decided per hop — all-streaming multiplies the bill for no visible gain, all-batch turns a revocation SLA into a fifteen-minute breach window

3. Which Write Wins | a batch replay of d-7712 at v4 racing a streaming write at v6, with the arrival time on a slider and the conflict rule on a toggle | last-writer-wins on (doc_id, version) gives the same answer at every delay; arrival order agrees with it on the happy path and silently reinstates stale content the moment the backfill lands late

4. Contracts On Arrows | the seven backbone contracts opened one at a time — schema, semantics, SLA, failure behavior — under two scenarios: swapping the embedding model, and serving reading the parser's internal rows | a swap moves two arrows and leaves five untouched; coupling to an implementation breaks stage 6 from a change at stage 3 with every schema still valid

5. Wipe And Rebuild | six stores you can wipe, plus a lossy-parser toggle, verdicting each as rebuilt-from-truth or gone-for-good | any derived store must survive being wiped and rebuilt from truth — the one that cannot has secretly become a source of truth, which is exactly what the dropped PDF tables were
